observation.visible_scene: A nighttime fireworks display filmed against a dark sky. Several golden-white radial bursts spread across the upper half of the frame at the start, accompanied by drifting smoke clouds, a diagonal power line crossing the scene, and a tree silhouette at the bottom right. Throughout the excerpt the bursts dim and fade while new bright linear trails and fan-shaped bursts appear, and the scene is repeatedly washed out by intense white flashes.
visible_changes: Frame 1 opens with multiple golden-white starburst clusters already expanded across the top sky, plus a bright white flash and smoke at the bottom center.
By frame 2 the bottom-center flash has faded, leaving the golden bursts to slowly dim; a magenta/red glow blooms inside the left cluster around frame 3.
A large bright white flash and smoke cloud erupts from the lower-left around frame 9 and recedes by frame 10, briefly overexposing the scene.
From about frame 12 onward, several short bright vertical/angled streaks appear along the bottom edge and grow upward through frames 16-27 (rising trails).
Another intense white flash fills much of the frame near frame 28, then subsides by frame 29.
After that flash the rising trails reach higher positions and open into fan-shaped golden bursts across the top of the sky (frames 29-41), with intermittent red glints.
Further bright flashes occur near frames 32, 36, and 39-40, each momentarily washing out the frame before the bursts re-emerge.
The original top-sky burst clusters fade to faint scattered dots by the middle of the clip while smoke continues to drift and accumulate.
The power line and tree silhouette shift position slightly between frames, indicating some handheld camera jitter or reframing.
outside_clip_unknowns: The launches that produced the initial bursts in frame 1 occurred before the excerpt.
The cause and type of the repeated bright white flashes (separate large bursts, ground effects, or a strobe) are not visible.
What happens to the display after frame 41 is unknown.
uncertain_details: Camera motion is uncertain: the diagonal power line and bottom tree appear at varying heights, which could be handheld tilt/pan or simply the flashes and smoke obscuring them.
Whether the lower bright linear streaks are ascending rockets that later burst at the top, or a result of camera reframing, cannot be fully separated from the background evidence.
The exact spatial relationship between the fading top bursts and the new top fan bursts is hard to confirm due to overexposed frames.
